items.title: Louis Armstrong and Herman Chittison Interview, 1960-05-04
items.q: we got the St. Louis blues we had a tenor sax man called Von El Pratt remember... when I got to Von El Pratt he's waiting with his tenor

ctx.x: I have a grin from ear to ear it's for a very good reason but this is probably one of the proudest moments in my career in the field of jazz and that is to have as a special guest on the program the man that I have always honestly considered to be the single most important person in the history of jazz and by that I mean Louie Armstrong and my voice is shaking as I try to introduce you and I should by this time not be you know frightened to introduce somebody but that's just the way I feel about it and I thought…

remember we was making this album and we got the St. Louis blues we had a tenor sax man called Von El Pratt remember and we didn't just say each man stand up know when they come in they wait for me to point to him you know and Chitteson took his blues and his solo Pete Deconje and when I got to Von El Pratt he's waiting with his tenor I said you take a dick eight balls went by four years ago but when he came down boy that cat blew a lot of heart didn't it Chitteson oh but he did just a man oh we we used to make…
didn't that uh sunnyside used to be one of your favorite records yeah it's still my favorite well because i've heard you talk about laughing louie also yeah favorite jimmy q
